claims.text: The catalyst is a platinum-based nanoscale catalyst with an ordered intermetallic structure and a high density of high-index facets.
The catalyst's high-index facets are maintained under a steady potential of 0.8 V versus RHE.
The controlled intervention is to replace a constant 0.8 V potential with cycling between 0.2 and 1.2 V versus RHE.
Ethanol oxidation is conducted in an aqueous medium at ambient temperature.
Complete ethanol oxidation involves a 12-electron and 12-proton transfer process.
Dynamic potential modulation induces reversible restructuring or reformation of high-index surface sites.
Dynamic potential modulation causes reversible shifts in the catalyst's surface oxidation state or electronic state.
Potential-induced restructuring modifies the geometry and electronic structure of active sites.
Changes in active-site geometry and electronic structure alter the adsorption strength of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
An intermediate adsorption strength that is neither too strong nor too weak can improve activation while limiting surface poisoning.
Dynamic restructuring reduces poisoning of the platinum-based catalyst during ethanol oxidation.
Dynamic restructuring accelerates multi-electron and proton-transfer steps in ethanol oxidation.
Potential cycling will increase ethanol-oxidation current density relative to operation at a constant 0.8 V.
Potential cycling will improve ethanol-oxidation product selectivity relative to operation at a constant 0.8 V.
Potential cycling will produce reversible FTIR and XAS signatures of changes in adsorbed intermediates and oxidation states.
The proposed enhancement should occur only under active ethanol-oxidation conditions in which cycling induces structural or electronic changes.
No enhancement should occur in the absence of ethanol or when applied potentials do not induce significant structural or electronic changes.
